notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.

Adapted canonical bedroom rule for a modern, minimal style. Prioritized clean circulation and open center as per brief. Added work_study and lounge_reading clusters as support options, activated by usefulness. Ensured storage options are balanced. Corrected tier_count_hints to use object_hints list format.

For 'work_study' and 'lounge_reading' clusters, 'keep_if_space_surplus' is set to true and 'drop_order_bias' to 'later' to reflect the 'prefer_open_center' and 'clean and minimal' style requirements. This allows these clusters to be included if there's comfortable surplus space, but they are candidates for dropping earlier if space becomes tight.

The 'utility_optional' cluster is set with 'keep_if_space_surplus' true and 'drop_order_bias' 'earliest' to ensure it's only included if there's significant surplus space, aligning with the minimal style.
Bed and nightstand counts are adjusted for typical bedroom configurations.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Bedroom correction raised restfulness and clutter control.
